label: CONNECTION

cover.headline: Reconnecting after *a busy season*
cover.sub: A new baby, a big job, a hard year: 5 ways back.

points.heading: Name the season out loud
points.body: Saying it was hard helps you both stop blaming each other for the distance.
points.panel: “This year has been a lot. I miss us.”

points.heading: Start smaller than you think
points.body: A full date night may feel like too much. Ten minutes counts.
points.panel: Sit together after the kids are asleep, phones in another room.

points.heading: Share the load you can see
points.body: Resentment grows when one person carries most of the invisible work.
points.panel: “Can we write down everything we’re each juggling?”

points.heading: Bring back one old ritual
points.body: Something you loved before life got so full.

points.heading: Be patient with the drift
points.body: Closeness returns gradually. Notice small signs it’s coming back.
points.panel: Each week, name one moment you felt close.

close.save: Save this for a season that’s too full.

caption:
Big seasons of life pull couples in different directions: a new baby, a demanding job, caring for a parent, a move.

The distance usually isn’t a sign that love has faded. It’s a sign you’ve been busy surviving. These five steps help you find your way back.

Save this, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
